title: The verdict on restore is derived differently from the live verdict (a latent bug)
problem: two implementations answer "is this match decided?" (the comment at `gameEngine.ts:1325` claims one). A free-for-all table whose vacated seat's `bot:<seat>` total reached the target persists live as running. After a restart the same row restores as `matchOver: true`, winner `bot:<seat>`.
proposed: split the fold. Restore calls `judgeMatch` with the same `SeatScoring` the live path builds. Alternatively, persist the verdict.
effect: One verdict path, so "restore disagrees with live" becomes impossible. `teamKeyMap` and `restoredMatchOver` are deleted.

title: A server rule mutates engine state outside the engine
problem: `gameTurn.ts:339-356` (`concedeRound`) writes `finishPosition`, `finishingOrder` and `roundOver` in place on `game.gameState`. It is a sibling of the engine's private `placeLastSeat` (`gameEngine.ts:668-673`). Proposed interface: `concedeRound(state, winnerSeat?: number): GameState` in the engine, returning a clone.
proposed: `concedeRound(state, winnerSeat?: number): GameState` in the engine, returning a clone.
effect: The placement rule (fewest cards first, seat as tiebreak) lives with the other placement rules. It becomes testable with no io.

title: The offline bot's exchange choice bypasses `autoMove.ts`, and the guard tests cannot see it
problem: CLAUDE.md's invariant says one module chooses a bot's move. Offline, that holds for plays only. The bot's exchange decision is made in a screen.
proposed: Move `pickGivebackCard` into `bot.ts`. The offline exchange-ready callback calls `runBotTurn()`. That goes through `offlineBotMove(state)`, which already reaches the exchange branch of `autoMoveForSeat`, because `initializeRematch` sets `currentTurnIndex` to the winner.
effect: Delete `givebackCardId`, `botGivebackCardId` and `exchangeIsStuck` from `app/game.tsx` (about 25 lines). Delete `GameContext.releaseStuckExchange` and the `useLocalExchange.releaseStuckExchange` field.
notes: GAME-RULES § Decisions "What the winner may hand back" names pickGivebackCard as in autoMove, which supports this finding.

title: The match lifecycle (start, fold a round, roll forward, deal next) has no module and exists three times
problem: The domain logic sits behind a React provider (the wrong seam), so it cannot be tested through an interface and gets copied instead. `initializeRematch(setup, mode, prevFinishingOrder, firstSeat)` leaks: It reads only `[0]` and `[last]` of the order. It silently falls back to seat 0 or the last seat when an id misses (`gameEngine.ts:876-880`).
proposed: The server keeps its own key mapping (F5) but calls `dealNextRound` and the same match start and roll-forward.
effect: About 70 mirrored lines leave `offlineMatch.ts`. The two state slots in `GameContext` and two `OfflineSave` fields (with their decode checks) go away.

title: `GameState` has no record of what just happened, so consumers diff fields and invent keys
problem: The UI depends on the engine's internal ordering of field writes, which is a leaky interface. Event identity is reconstructed heuristically, and the harness has to search for key collisions. Online and offline derive "an exchange was given" in two different ways (a state diff versus the callback site), which is part of why F1 exists.
proposed: Interface: interface LastMove { seq: number; seat: number; kind: "deal" | "play" | "pass" | "giveback" | "stuckRelease"; closedTrick: boolean }
effect: Turn and bot keys become `lastMove.seq`, so collisions are impossible and the collision harness can be deleted. `trickClosedWithWinner`, `prevPassCountRef`, `prevTrickClosedRef` and the three online refs collapse to reading `lastMove`.

title: The stuck-exchange safety valve is kept at three sites for a state the rules make unreachable in a dealt round
problem: Why it is unreachable: `getValidGivebackCards` (`gameEngine.ts:987-998`) falls back to the lowest card for any non-empty eligible hand. A just-dealt winner holds at least 13 cards plus the one received. The valve is kept at: `autoMove.ts:89` (`resolveStuckExchange`) `app/game.tsx:147-155` `GameContext.tsx:270-273` plus `tests/server/stuckExchange.test.ts` Proposal: keep one valve inside the engine's giveback transition, if any is wanted for corrupted restores, and delete the UI and context paths.
proposed: keep one valve inside the engine's giveback transition, if any is wanted for corrupted restores, and delete the UI and context paths. This folds into F1.
effect: the bench stops being a silent sibling that keeps old semantics after the fix.
notes: GAME-RULES § Decisions "What the winner may hand back" makes the stuck state unreachable by rule, consistent with removing the extra valves.

title: `FoldRoundInput` is a wide, closure-based interface with dead flexibility
problem: the interface is shallow relative to its implementation. The caller has to understand how the closures interact, including the default chaining and that frozen keys are never nameable.
proposed: Replace the closures with data: `foldRoundIntoMatch(round, ledger, seats: SeatScoring[])`, where `SeatScoring` is `{ engineId, key, team?, frozenKey?, crownable }`.
effect: `accumulates` is deleted. The server's policy becomes data and can be tested by value.

title: The team has two sources of truth
problem: `Player.team` is optional and supplied by callers. Every caller must remember `teamForSeat`: `app/lobby.tsx:152` and `:180` (on count change and on mode change) `tableState.ts:107` `dealVotedRound` strips team outside teams mode (`tableHandlers.ts:371`) `bot.ts:148-156` ignores `Player.team` and recomputes from `teamForSeat`. Scoring reads `p.team` (`GameContext.tsx:88-91`, `onlineGameLogic.ts:359-362`, `scorePill.ts`, `matchState.isDrawnRound`).
proposed: `initializeGame` and `dealNextRound` derive `team = teamForSeat(seat, n, gameMode)`, and `SeatSetup` drops `team`.
effect: four caller sites lose team plumbing, and a player whose team disagrees with the mode becomes impossible.
notes: GAME-RULES § Decisions on teams (draw) is unaffected; this only moves where team is derived.

title: "What the table demands of the seat on move" is derived in five places, and `startCard`/`firstPlayMade` encode one obligation in two fields
problem: "What the table demands of the seat on move" is derived in five places (checkSelection at gameEngine.ts:490, autoMove.ts:97-103, stagedPlay.ts:40-45, GameTable.tsx:1620, offlineMatch's weakestBeatingPlay). `getAllValidPlays` takes a redundant `isNewTrick`/`lastPlayed` pair, and `startCard`/`firstPlayMade` encode one opening obligation in two fields, which forces the `playedRanks` inference in `openingIsPending` and `roundUnplayed`.
proposed: `GameState.openingCard: Card | null` replaces `startCard` and `firstPlayMade`; add `tableDemand(state): { toBeat; mustInclude }` and `legalPlays(state, seat)`, and give `getAllValidPlays` a `toBeat` plus optional `mustInclude`.
effect: Five derivations become one. The `isNewTrick` parameter is gone.

title: Three transitions use three error modes, and every caller pre-checks
problem: `processPlay` throws (`assertPlayable`, `:690-710`). `processPass` returns its input when refused (`:788`). `processExchangeChoice` returns its input with no reason code (`:949-978`).
proposed: `processPlay` keeps its throwing floor internally.
effect: `tableHandlers` `playAction`, `passAction` and `exchangeAction` (`:198-301`, about 100 lines) shrink to about 40. `GameContext`'s three callbacks become one `act(move)`.

title: `autoMoveForSeat` reports its result through a callback and an in-place mutation; achievement flags are recorded at three sites
problem: `autoMove.ts:54-69` and `105-143`: `ctx.onMove` and `ctx.roundFlags` are mutated. The server wraps it just to recover the move (`gameTurn.ts:118-131`) and computes `wasExchange` beforehand (`:293`). `recordPlayFlags` runs at `autoMove.ts:124` and `:138`, and in `tableHandlers.ts:234` through a pass-through wrapper (`gameTurn.ts:104-106`).
proposed: Pure. `commitMove(io, game, next, move)` records the flags and the replay from `move` at one site.
effect: `AutoMoveContext`, the server wrapper and the `recordPlayFlags` wrapper are deleted. A forgotten-flags path becomes impossible.

title: Type weaknesses that make callers carry invariants
problem: `playedRanks?` stays optional "for a round persisted before the tally existed" (`gameEngine.ts:103-112`). Both stores are version-gated: `GAME_SCHEMA_VERSION=3` and `OFFLINE_SAVE_VERSION=3`. Every reader still handles `undefined`: `bot.ts:46-51`, `openingIsPending`, `roundUnplayed`, `processPlay:745`.
proposed: one shared `parseGameState(unknown): { ok: true; state: GameState } | { ok: false; reason }` at the restore seam, with required fields. `ExchangePhase` is a set of flags with optional cards (`:58-77`). The phase is never cleared, so its `.active` is checked at 70 sites in 15 files.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: Pass-throughs (each fails the deletion test)
problem: `lib/exchangeCeremony.ts` (`exchangeAnnounceMs` equals `exchangeAnnounceFrom`) `server/game/replayShape.ts:30` (`startReplayLog` returns `[]`) `gameTurn.ts:104-106` (the `recordPlayFlags` wrapper) `onlineGameLogic.ts:324` (`ScoreboardRow = ScoreLine`)
proposed: inline it into the server callers, or move it to server/game.
effect: one less file, and one less false comment.

title: Bot seat-key format is defined twice
problem: three spellings of one key format. A change to one leaves rating unable to recognise bots.
proposed: move botSeat.ts into lib/game (it has no server dependencies). rating.ts and onlineGameLogic then import `botSeatKey`/`isBotSeatKey`.
effect: one home; delete the constant and the inline template.

title: Non-domain modules sit inside `lib/game`
problem: `sharedGameFlow.ts` imports `react` (`useExchangeAnnouncement`) in a folder that otherwise loads under `node --test`. `roundEnding.ts`, `matchEnding.ts`, `exchangeTimeline.ts` and `dealTimeline.ts` are animation worklets. The server imports `exchangeTimeline.ts` for `exchangeGiveDelayMs` and pulls the pose geometry in with it.
proposed: Keep only rules in `lib/game`. Move the wire types to `shared/protocol.ts`. Split the exchange and deal timing into a timing-only module the server imports.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.
conflicts: CLAUDE.md invariant naming gameEngine.ts as the rules home constrains what may move out.

title: The placement-points rule is duplicated
problem: `server/game/stats.ts:33-35` (`pointsForPlacement`, "mirroring … `scoreRound` exactly"). Proposal: export `placementPoints(placement, n)` from the engine and use it in both places.
proposed: Export `placementPoints(placement, n)` from the engine and use it in both `scoreRound` and `server/game/stats.ts`.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: `botChoosePlay` takes nine positional parameters, five of them optional
problem: `bot.ts:221-231`. The only production caller assembles them from `GameState` (`autoMove.ts:110-122`). 31 test calls read like `botChoosePlay(me, null, true, [8,8,8], undefined, () => 0.5, false, playedRanks)`.
proposed: Add `botView(state, seat): BotView` and make it `botChoosePlay(view: BotView, rng)`.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: `gameEngine.ts` is a 1525-line module with about ten responsibilities
problem: `gameEngine.ts` is 1525 lines with about ten responsibilities (cards and deck, combinations and beat rules, legal plays, trick state machine, display helpers, exchange, opening predicates, teams and deal rotation, round construction, match scoring, plus a transport timeout). 16 exports have no production caller and exist only for tests, which therefore reach past the interface.
proposed: Split into `cards`, `combinations`, `legalPlays`, `round`, `exchange` and `match` files under `lib/game/`, move display helpers to `lib/cardNames.ts`, un-export the internals and re-point their tests at `checkSelection`/`legalPlays`/`foldRoundIntoMatch`. Reword the CLAUDE.md rules-home invariant first.
effect: Locality: each rule area is one file, and the test-only export surface (tests-T15's 17 exports) disappears.
conflicts: CLAUDE.md invariant "Before changing a game rule — it lives in lib/game/gameEngine.ts": splitting the module needs that invariant reworded to name lib/game.

title: Time and dealing randomness are only partly injected (several clocks)
problem: `gameTimers.ts:12-29` has an injectable `Clock` (`setClock`), used for AFK, grace and `secondsUntil`. These still read wall time: `onlineGameLogic.ts:95, 124` default `now = Date.now()` for `markExchangeSettled`/`visibleExchangePhase`, and `gamePersistence.ts:86-89, 219` never pass `now`. Under `fakeClock`, `turnSecondsRemaining` uses fake time while exchange-card visibility uses real time.
proposed: Add `clock: Clock` and `deal?: (playerCount: number, firstSeat: number) => Card[][]` to `TableDeps` (F1). Pass `deps.clock.now()` into `visibleExchangePhase`/`markExchangeSettled` and into `roomStore.claimRoomSeat`/`getRoomSeatHolds` as a `now` argument. `seatForClaim` already takes `now`.
effect: Exchange-ceremony timing and seat-hold expiry become testable with `fakeClock` instead of real sleeps. Exchange-path tests can deal a fixed hand instead of looping.
notes: 09-tests-server-engine refines server-F9 and tests-T8: a Clock already exists for five timer kinds (server/game/gameTimers.ts:9-32, tests/helpers/fakeClock.ts; landed by closed #1600). What is missing is integration-harness wiring plus the state-ack and seat-hold timers. tests-T8's configuration half is covered by the env-at-import entry.

title: The db module captures DATABASE_URL at import, which shapes the whole integration tree
problem: The test server's interface hides the real seam, which is which database the modules talk to. A test cannot import a store statically. Each file re-derives a connection to the schema.
proposed: Have `startTestServer()` return its `db` and `pool` handles, for example `server.db` and `server.query(sql)`. Make server/db build lazily from a `createDb(url)` that the server boot owns, not from module scope. Dynamic imports then become static, ad-hoc pools are deleted, and one process can boot N servers.
effect: About 25 pool constructions and 33 dynamic-import blocks are deleted. Several files can merge (the harness trio).

title: Deal randomness cannot be injected
problem: `shuffleDeck` and `dealCards` read `globalThis.crypto` (`gameEngine.ts:229-263`). Tests and scripts monkeypatch the global instead: `tests/helpers/offlineMatch.ts` (`withSeededDeals`, including the "non-configurable getter in some Node builds" workaround) `tests/native/setup.ts` `tests/e2e/helpers/seededRandomness.ts` `scripts/measureHeadsUpBalance.ts` Workarounds grew into the interface: `initializeGame(..., dealt?)` with validation at `:1124-1137`, and `initializeRematch(..., dealtHands?)`. …
proposed: `type RandomSource = { getRandomValues(a: Uint32Array): Uint32Array }`, with: `dealCards(n, firstSeat, random = cryptoRandom)` `initializeGame(setup, mode, { firstSeat, random, dealt })`
effect: the global patching in four places is deleted, and seeded reproduction becomes an argument.

title: Shutdown hands rooms back while bot and AFK timers keep playing and persisting
problem: `beginShutdown()` (`shutdown.ts:74`) only sets a flag. The flag is read by the rejoin, the orphan sweep, the router and the lobby grace (`tableHandlers.ts:661,813,819`, `tableRouter.ts:294`, `socketTable.ts:248`, `socketPresence.ts:196`). It is never read by the turn timers.
proposed: Stop all turn timers in the shutdown path before `closeOwnership()`. One option is to call `clearRoomTimers(roomId)` for every `activeGames` key inside `beginShutdown()`. Alternatively, make `arm()` in `gameTimers.ts` refuse while `isShuttingDown()`.
effect: One owner per row holds through a deploy. Add a test that fires a bot timer after `beginShutdown` and asserts no write.

title: Lobby grace lives in one process, so a player who reconnects to another instance loses the seat
problem: ADR-0003 makes multi-instance real, but lobby grace is a per-process timer. Suppose a player drops on instance A and reconnects within the grace window through instance B. A's expiry asks A's own `userSocketMap`, which does not hold the player.
proposed: Make the expiry ask the cluster instead of its own maps. `isUserAtTable(userId, roomId)` already exists in `socketRegistry.ts:61` and uses `io.in(userRoom).fetchSockets()`. Then `if (await isUserAtTable(userId, roomId)) return;` replaces the local check.
effect: Removes a cross-instance seat-loss class. Deletes the false comment.
notes: ADR-0003 makes multi-instance load-bearing, so a per-process grace is a real cross-instance defect.

title: `active_games` persistence has no owning module, so tests mock drizzle internals
problem: One table's lifecycle (write order, delete order, "room_players has no cascade so it goes first") is spread over three modules and raw drizzle. Tests reach past every interface to substitute it: `t.mock.method(db.query.activeGames, "findFirst", …)` appears 6× in `tableStalls.test.ts` (94, 113, 279, 291, 303, 321), plus `endMatchVote.test.ts:269` and `persistedEnvelope.test.ts:147`. `t.mock.method(db, "delete", …)` appears at `persistedEnvelope.test.ts:148`.
proposed: `pruneStaleRooms` and `deleteUser`'s room purge should share one `roomStore.purgeRooms(tx, ids)` that encodes the delete order once.
effect: Deletes about 15 `mock.method(db…|persistence…)` calls. `rehydrateGame` and `resumeOrphanedTables` stop importing `db` and `shared/schema` (`tableHandlers.ts:42-43,49`).

title: `tableHandlers.ts` (839 lines) is a god module
problem: `tableHandlers.ts` (839 lines) holds refusal helpers, rehydrate, move validation, voting and next-round dealing, rejoin, startMatch, seat loss, the dispatcher and a sweeper. Next-round construction exists twice (`dealVotedRound` vs `tableState.newTable`, with different team rules) and the ready gate has two arithmetics (`votesUnanimous` vs `startMatchAction`).
proposed: Pure deciders `tableMoves.decideMove`, `tableVotes.castRematch`/`readyGate`, `tableState.nextRound`, plus `tableLifecycle` and `seatPresence` modules; `tableHandlers.ts` keeps only an ~80-line dispatcher applying decisions through `TableDeps`.
effect: Move legality, vote gates and round construction become unit-testable as pure functions, with no stub io and no db mock. The two-arithmetic bug class for vote gates disappears.
notes: Closed #1597 (one move-commit path, typed validate()) may be partial progress; re-measure before cutting.

title: The game layer's output port is the raw Socket.IO server
problem: The interface the game logic needs is small: "send to room", "send to user", "send state with one retry on a missing ack", and "who is online". The interface it actually takes is all of Socket.IO. Tests have to recreate it by hand.
proposed: There would be one Socket.IO adapter built in `setupSocket`, plus a recording adapter in `tests/helpers`. The router (`tableRouter.ts`) keeps `io` for `serverSideEmit`, because it really is transport.
effect: About 44 `io` params collapse into one `deps`. 12 hand-rolled stubs become one recording outbox.

title: An ownership query error during reclaim is read as "claimed elsewhere" and drops live tables
problem: `takeLock` returns `null` when it cannot connect, but `false` when the query throws (`:149-151`). `reclaim` treats `false` as lost (`:170-173`). It deletes the room from `held` and disposes the game.
proposed: Return `null` from the `catch` so the existing `OWNERSHIP_RECLAIM_RETRY_MS` path covers it. This is a one-line change.
effect: Removes a data-loss path on DB failure. Add a unit test with a query that throws once.

title: `disposeGame` releases the lock before the row delete lands
problem: `void releaseRoom(roomId)` (`:116`) runs right away, while the `active_games` delete is queued behind pending writes on `inRoomOrder` (`:117-124`). In that window, a restore-mode action such as rejoin or a rematch vote can find no owner, claim the lock and rehydrate the row it reads. That resurrects a table that was just disposed.
proposed: When `deleteRow` is set, release inside the same `inRoomOrder` chain after the delete settles: `void inRoomOrder(roomId, () => del().finally(() => releaseRoom(roomId)))`.
effect: Closes a resurrection race. `activeGames` is already empty, so nothing else waits on it.

title: Retention and prune deletes are unbounded under a 5 s statement timeout, and one policy has two homes
problem: Each sweep is one unbatched `DELETE ... WHERE ts < cutoff`. Once a backlog makes it exceed the 5 s `statement_timeout`, it times out on every run and never catches up.
proposed: Use one batched helper, `pruneOlderThan(table, where, batch=5000)`, as a `DELETE ... WHERE ctid IN (SELECT ctid ... LIMIT n)` loop.
effect: The sweep converges after an outage, and the handshake loses a write. `retention.ts` becomes the only home again.

title: HTTP rate limiters use the per-instance memory store
problem: No `store` is passed, so express-rate-limit keeps counts in process memory. Under ADR-0003 with N instances: the per-username login limit becomes about 10 × N attempts per window, and every deploy resets it. That matters because the comment at `routes.ts:139-149` calls this limiter what actually makes a password hard to guess.
proposed: Use a Postgres-backed store for the auth limiters only. A small `Store` over one `rate_limits(key, window_start, hits)` table using upsert is enough; the other limiters can stay in memory. Otherwise, record the N× ceiling as accepted in `server/CLAUDE.md`.
effect: The brute-force bound becomes cluster-wide and survives restarts.
notes: ADR-0003 (multi-instance) makes a per-instance memory store a real gap.

title: The lobby port is half adopted
problem: inconsistent seam placement. Half the lobby can be tested with `node --test` and no Postgres; the other half needs integration tests (`quickmatchAutoStart.test.ts`, `lobbyGrace.test.ts`).
proposed: `rejoinRoomIntent(port, {code})`, `setVisibilityIntent(port, {visibility})` and `quickmatchIntent(port, {maxPlayers, gameMode})`. Quickmatch reuses `joinRoomIntent`'s claim-and-announce and `createRoomIntent({visibility:"public", autoStart:true})`. Widen `LobbyPort.store` accordingly.
effect: about 60 lines of duplication removed, with all 6 lobby intents behind one port.

title: A safeguard exempts a file that breaks its rule
problem: The scan's list is hand-maintained, so it silently exempts the third handler family. The local path only fires when the connecting instance is also the owner, because the grace timer was armed on the owner (`tableHandlers.ts:713`) and `clearDisconnectGrace` is local. The routed `game:rejoin`, whose `rejoinAction` clears the grace (494), already covers the general case.
proposed: delete the local block in `announcePresence` and rely on the routed rejoin. Alternatively, make the scan cover every `server/socket/*` file. Encapsulate `activeGames`: export `getGame`/`hasGame` from the table runtime (F13) rather than the raw `Map`.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.
notes: A self-exempting safeguard in the CLAUDE.md "No self-defeating safeguards" sense.

title: The connect path and the sweeper fetch every socket in the cluster
problem: Every connection, every `friend:get_online_list`, and every orphan or sweeper pass calls `io.fetchSockets()` over the whole cluster. Through the postgres adapter, that is a broadcast request whose reply holds every socket. A reconnect storm after a deploy is therefore O(N²) in sockets.
proposed: `onlineUserIds(ids)` → `io.in(ids.map(userRoom)).fetchSockets()`, and `tablePresence(roomId)` → `io.in(roomId).fetchSockets()`.
effect: The cost becomes proportional to friends or seats, not to the cluster.
notes: ADR-0003 multi-instance.

title: `routes.ts` (1041 lines) is a god module, with repeated auth and session plumbing
problem: `routes.ts` (1041 lines) mixes 12 limiter definitions, session and mail helpers, auth and recovery, account, friends, stats, admin, ladders, replays, reports and creating the `http.Server`. `req.session.userId!` appears 26 times, the getUser-then-401 check 5 times with inconsistent codes (`/me` answers USER_NOT_FOUND), and the regenerate/revoke/save session sequence is duplicated in register and login.
proposed: A `routeTable.ts` with `RouteSpec { method, path, access: public|signedIn|admin, limiters, body, handle }` and `mount(app, routes)`, an `accountSession.signIn`/`hashPassword`, and per-area files `routes/{auth,account,friends,ladder,replays,reports,admin}.ts`; keep each route's reply timing and do not merge the recovery state machine.
effect: Removes 26 non-null assertions and the `/me` inconsistency, shrinks register and login by about 25 lines each, and keeps each area file under about 250 lines.
notes: Respects the CONTEXT.md rejection of consolidating the account-recovery blocks (ADR-0007); the split must not re-propose it.

title: Mutate→broadcast→persist→arm is repeated, and the `RoundOverWriters` seam is bypassed
problem: Ordering is documented as load-bearing: settle before serving (`gamePersistence.ts:217-219`), persist before dispose (`roundOver.ts:170-174`). Yet the sequence is open-coded at each site. The one injected seam leaks, so a test with fake writers still hits Postgres.
proposed: `RoundOverWriters` folds into `TableDeps`, so one injection point covers every path.
effect: about 6 open-coded sequences become 1, the 3 close-table copies become 1, and the writers leak disappears.

title: `OnlineGameState` is mutated by many modules; only seat fields have a ledger
problem: the vote and score invariants ("cleared whenever the roster changes or a round deals") are spread across 4 modules. `seatLedger` shows the fix works.
proposed: extend the ledger pattern to a `matchLedger.ts` covering `castRematchVote`, `clearVotes`, `foldRound(result)`, `rollForward()` and `markEndedByVote()`. Pin "only the ledgers write these fields" with the same scan `seatLedger.test.ts` uses.
effect: vote and score lifecycle rules move into one file and can be tested on a bare object.
notes: Open #1640 (tableState field list complete by type) and closed #1598/#1599 (table pack/unpack, seat ledger) touch the same state; re-check scope.

title: Layering: `game/` imports `socket/`, and cycles are dodged with mutable module setters
problem: the directories don't reflect dependency direction, and the mutable setters are ambient global wiring that tests must reset (`reopenOwnership`, `installTableHandlers` in every table test's `before`).
proposed: with F1, `createTableRuntime(deps: TableDeps): { apply(action): Promise<IntentReply>; rehydrate(...) }` is constructed once in `setupSocket` and passed to the router. The setter globals go away. Move the shared utilities (`logger`, `payload`) to `server/shared/`.
effect: removes 3 of the 4 setters, and the import graph points one way (socket → game → store).

title: Outbound HTTP has no timeout
problem: `fetch` to the mail provider and to Expo push has no `signal`, so a hung remote holds the request, or the un-awaited invite push, forever. `mail.ts:101-104` cites the Replit "Run button", which has been stale since ADR-0006.
proposed: Add `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000)` to both, and delete the stale sentence.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: The shutdown budget leaves out steps it spends time on
problem: `FORCED_EXIT_MS = 1500 + 6000 + 2000` counts the settle, the drain and slack. It omits `socketAdapterReady(1_000)`, `io.close()`, `closeOwnership()` and `adapterPool.end()`. Only about 1 s of the 2 s slack is really free, and the test checks just the drain against the watchdog.
proposed: Derive `FORCED_EXIT_MS` from a named list of step budgets, and have the test sum that list.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: The deal waits on a best-effort status write
problem: `await roomStore.updateRoomStatus(...).catch(warn)` sits before `broadcastGameState`. The write is explicitly optional, yet under DB stress it delays the deal by up to the connection wait plus the query timeout.
proposed: Make it `void` (fire-and-forget), or move it after the emits.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: The error recorder amplifies DB outages, and client crashes inflate server errors
problem: Each error-level log line runs one `INSERT server_errors`. During a DB outage, every failed query logs an error, and each log asks for another pool checkout. That deepens the pool starvation it is reporting.
proposed: Have the recorder drop inserts while the pool has waiters, or keep a small in-memory ring and flush it from the sweeper. Log client crashes at warn level. Give bug reports their own limiter instance.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: `/admin` and the circle leaderboard saturate the 10-connection pool
problem: `adminSnapshot` runs 18 queries in parallel against a pool of 10. The error-group queries are GROUP BYs over the whole table, despite the claim at `admin.ts:8` that "Every query is bounded". `symbolicate` parses a source map per crash group on the game process's event loop.
proposed: Bound the error groups with a date window. Run the admin queries in chunks of at most 4. Replace the per-member `currentRow` with one `inArray` query.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: Boot DDL runs without a lock while another revision serves
problem: `ensureSchema` runs about 100 `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` statements on every boot. Postgres takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the table even when the column exists.
proposed: Wrap the DDL in `pg_advisory_xact_lock(<const>)` with `SET LOCAL lock_timeout` and a retry, or skip `ALTER`s whose column is already in `information_schema`.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: `pruneStaleRooms` only knows about this process's games
problem: Candidates are filtered with the local `activeGames.has(id)` only. A room older than `STALE_ROOM_MAX_AGE_MS` that is live on another instance loses its `room_players` and `active_games` rows underneath that instance. The comment at `:290` claims a safety it only has on a single instance.
proposed: Exclude rooms with `status = 'in_progress'` or an `active_games.updated_at` within the window in SQL. That makes the guard cluster-wide.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: An uncaught exception exits without draining queued persists

proposed: Call the existing `shutdown("uncaughtException", ...)` with a short watchdog, then exit with code 1.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: Reduce-motion opens one native subscription per subscriber
problem: on native, `subscribeSystemReduceMotion` adds an `AccessibilityInfo` listener and fires an `isReduceMotionEnabled()` bridge call for every subscriber. Every CardView subscribes, so one table mount opens about 54 native listeners and bridge calls for one boolean.
proposed: a module store with one native listener, ref-counted, and a cached value. `useSyncExternalStore` readers share it, following the pattern already used for the in-app setting in the same file.
effect: one listener per app; no bridge burst on deal.

title: GIOCA's refusal ladder re-implements the engine's rule outside `gameEngine.ts`
problem: `readStagedPlay` already calls `checkSelection`, which returns `{ok:false, code}` (stagedPlay.ts:57-61). It then throws `code` away and asks `playButtonLabel` again. `playButtonLabel` is a second copy of `beatRefusal`'s ladder (royal, bomb, type, length, tooLow), working on a lossy `ComboShape`.
proposed: `PlayButtonLabel` becomes `"play" | SelectionRefusal`. Equivalent wherever the label is read: `selectionLeaves.tsx:117-140` reads `reason` only when `!staged.playable`.
effect: Deletes about 50 lines (`playButtonLabel` and `ComboShape`). `turnTimerUi.ts` goes back to what its header says it is.
notes: #1596 is closed, but 01-table and 02-components re-verified that stagedPlay still discards check.code and asks playButtonLabel (kept both functions plus a parity test), so it is not fixed.

title: Hand-row geometry is buried in `StraightHand`, computed in three parallel loops; the tested hit-test is a decoy
problem: All of this is pure arithmetic (card size per turn, crop, arc solve, tilt overhang, `topClearance`, `heldCeiling`, slot, home and shift per card, strips, rotated hit test). It is locked inside a 22-prop memo component, so only a renderer or Playwright can reach it. The same per-card values are derived three times: `restY` at 1330 equals `y0` at 1085 (`rowBase + crop + home.y - cardH/2`).
proposed: A JSX-free `components/handLayout.ts` with `layoutHandRow(input): HandRowLayout` (card size, crop, arc, clearance, slots and per-card places) and a worklet `cardUnder(layout, x, y, shown, reduceMotion)`; `StraightHand` renders from it and `handTurnScale` imports it instead of re-implementing it.
effect: `StraightHand` drops about 200 lines of arithmetic, and the three loops become one. `handTurnScale` imports the real function instead of copying it.

title: The exchange's presentation is smeared across five modules, with GameTable holding its state machine
problem: No module owns "the exchange as the table shows it". GameTable keeps the stage-report state (`reported`, `exchangeSeq`, the render-time seq bump at 503) and derives `stages`, `choiceReady`, `exchangeIsMine`, `choiceOpen`, chip text, pile note, seat lit and shift, and giveable. ExchangeLegs reports stages back up through two callbacks, and the hand reads stages again via `useHandArrival`.
proposed: Interface: export function exchangeNotes(i: { shown: ExchangeAnnounceData|null; stages: ExchangeStages; view: ExchangeView; giveable?: Card[]; viewerSeat: number; spectating: boolean; nameOf: (s:number)=>string; t: TFn })
effect: About 90 lines leave GameTable, and the exchange's derivations sit in one file. `exchangeNotes` is a node test table (two-Jokers, receive at rest, give at rest, fallback giveback, watcher).
notes: 01-table: ui-F3 has only line drift; the two sentences also differ in grammatical person and leg selection.

title: Table geometry is a 12-field bag mixed with game state, fanned out field by field, and the layout is encoded twice
problem: `SeatGeometry` mixes frame geometry (scale, window, table edges, surplus, bottomPad, handCardH) with game state (players, opponents, viewerSeat). `ThrownPlayInput`'s own doc (flightPhysics.ts:560-565) says the fields are spread because naming a per-render object inside an effect trips `exhaustive-deps`. The interface shape is a workaround for missing memoisation.
proposed: `usePileFlight({ ...state, layout, seating, ... })`: the dependency list goes from 25 to about 12. Optional second step (L, high risk): render the top, side and centre sections at `layout.boxes` (absolute) so flexbox and the model cannot disagree.
effect: About 60 lines of field-forwarding go across GameTable, pile, deal, dealSlots and ExchangeLegs. One anchors computation per render.

title: Opponent seats: two near-identical slot components rendered three times with 13 identical props
problem: The slots' 12-prop interface is as big as their bodies (shallow). GameTable repeats the same 11-13 prop expressions per seat (`onMove(seat)`, `seatCount(...)`, `deal.arrivalsFor(seat)`, `passed.includes(seat)`, `vacatedOf`, `disconnectedSeats[seat]`, `seatCountdown`, `focusMode`, `seatMark(seat)`). About 60 lines of JSX that must change in three places.
proposed: Primitives stay primitive, so the memo still holds.
effect: About 70 lines removed from seats.tsx and about 60 from GameTable. "Fixed the top seat, forgot the sides" becomes impossible.

title: Hand-written memo comparators, with a source-parsing test to keep them complete
problem: Both comparators are shallow equality except for `card` (compared by id) and two mount-only props. Adding a prop and forgetting a line is a silent stale-card bug. The guard is a regex over interface text that breaks if the interface is restyled (e.g.
proposed:
Interface: export function propsEqualExcept

(by: { [K in keyof P]?: ((a: P[K], b: P[K]) => boolean) | 'ignore' }) : (a: P, b: P) => boolean; // iterates the union of both objects' keys; Object.is for the rest
effect: About 55 comparator lines are deleted, and so is the source-parsing test, replaced by a 5-case unit test of `propsEqualExcept`. A new prop is compared by default, so the forgotten-line class is gone.

title: Turn presentation: two parallel 5-way ternaries and two `turnTimerActive` calls in GameTable's JSX
problem: This is pure presentation logic inline in render. A branch added to one ladder and not the other makes the screen-reader sentence diverge from the chip. The two timer questions differ only in three inputs.
proposed: A pure `turnPresentation(input)` in `components/turnTimerUi.ts` returning `{ chip: { key, params, spokenKey }, clock: { active, resetKey, seconds }, seat? }`, so the chip text and the spoken sentence share one decision.
effect: About 50 lines out of the JSX. A node test table replaces the native mounts that today pin the chip text (`matchTurnChip`, `dealTurn`).

title: OS orientation lock lives in the table component
problem: A true-external dependency (UIKit/Android orientation plus a custom native module) is driven from inside the presentational table. The adapter's quirks (#1211, #1378) sit next to card logic. It is the only `ScreenOrientation` use in `components/`.
proposed: `export function useLandscapeLock(navigation?: NavigationLike): void` in `lib/device/orientation.tsx`.
effect: About 40 lines and 3 imports leave GameTable. `orientationFirstRender.test.tsx` and `orientationRows.test.tsx` can target the hook, and future orientation fixes do not touch GameTable.

title: "The play that ended the round has landed" is decided four times, behind a call-order contract
problem: Each hook re-derives "ended, nothing in flight, nothing pending" from `timeline.inFlight` and `timeline.pending()`. Each carries the same prose contract: it must be called after `usePileFlight`, because `pending()` is read at call time. That ordering is enforced by comment only.
proposed: `usePileFlight` (the module that owns the throw) returns `endedLanding(ended: boolean): number | null`, the landing time of the ending play or null. Alternatively, `tableTimeline` gains `landedSince(at: number): number | null`. The two hooks take that landing time as input instead of `timeline`, which also removes the ordering contract.
effect: Two copies of the gate and two ordering comments are deleted. A new ending consumer cannot read `pending()` before the throw is registered.

title: The lamp level has three writers that guess ownership from the target value
problem: Three effects write one `lvlT`. Two infer "this level is mine" by comparing the current target with their own constant, and the third does no inference at all. Example: a link that drops and recovers during a lost round's dim resets the level to 1 and ends the dim early.
proposed: In `lampControls`: `hold(s, owner: "lost" | "breath" | "link", level: number | null, rate)`. `Lamp` carries `holds: Record<owner, number>`, and the effective target is `min(1, …holds)`. `setLevel` leaves the public `LampRig` and is replaced by `hold`.
effect: The two sentinel comparisons go. Each writer releases only its own hold.

title: CardView carries an interaction model that only the tutorial uses
problem: CardView is two modules in one. One paints a face or back with its a11y label. The other is a press and selection interaction: a spring lift of `-14` when `selected`, plus a press rise and tilt.
proposed: make CardView a pure painter (face/back + a11y). Move press and lift into a `TutorialCard` wrapper next to its only caller, or have the tutorial reuse the hand's lift via `handRowHeadroom`. Then `noLift` goes away.
effect: the interface narrows (`noLift`, `onPress`, `selected` leave the painter). The table stops paying for per-card animation state it never uses.

title: `flightPhysics.ts` is a grab bag whose name misleads, guarded by an import-ownership scan
problem: Low cohesion; the name misleads on half its contents. `flightHooks.test.ts` pins "each helper has one component owner" by regex over import lines, which is a substitute for module boundaries. Real duplication: `readThrownPlay` 588-594 and `readExchangeLegs` 630-633 carry the identical "own hand slot, else `HAND_SCALE/FIELD_SCALE` at the seat" expression.
proposed: `impact.ts`: tiers, trauma, flinch, shake, flare, `landWobble`. `tableLayout.ts`: anchors (F4). `passes.ts`: `comboKey`, `trickClosedWithWinner`, `passedSeats`, `seatsJustPassed`.
effect: `flightHooks.test.ts` is deleted. Each test file in `flightPhysics.test.ts` maps to one module.

title: Three hand-rolled countdowns; the seat ring and the turn chip show the same window from independent clocks
problem: The same concept ("a server window of N seconds, restarted by a key, optionally held") is implemented three ways. GameTable's comment (1086-1094) says the ring "sweeps over the same window the viewer's chip counts down". The two run on unrelated timers (interval ticks against an animation duration plus `Date.now` accumulation), and their hold semantics are implemented separately.
proposed: The ring drives its `withTiming` from `seconds*1000 - elapsedMs()`; the chip and the mark render `left`. Pure core: `countdownStep(state, now)`.
effect: About 60 lines are replaced by one tested hook. The chip and ring cannot drift by construction.

title: `CardItem` has 30 props, a boolean disguised as a number, and two "deal" mechanisms
problem: `dealDelay` is documented as "ms to wait, or -1", but its only caller passes `descending ? 0 : -1` (1355). It is a boolean, and `dealDelayRef`/`withDelay` always wait 0.
proposed: `pose` becomes `poseOf(entry, state, now)` with one call site feeding style, rect and the landing reaction.
effect: The props become about 12 grouped values, and the comparator shrinks (pairs with F8). The descend duration moves to `Motion` (`Motion.exchange.*`) instead of a component literal.

title: Notice float, opening gate and veils are state machines written as render-time `setState`
problem: The float reducer tracks four "last seen" values (`passSeen`, `errorSeen`, `autoSeen`, `withdrawnSeen`) inline. Its only tests are native mounts (`passMarker`, `onlineErrorFloat`, `offlineAutoPass`, `onlineAutoPass`). The veil decision is five booleans with long comments.
proposed: Pure `nextFloat(prev, input)` in `components/table/tableFloat.ts` and `tableVeils(input): Record<VeilRole, boolean>` plus a `VeilRegion` component in `tableVeils.ts`; the veil test then keys on `<VeilRegion>` instead of indentation.
effect: About 60 lines of render-phase logic become two tested pure functions. The whitespace-sensitive scan goes away.

title: GIOCA and PASSA each hand-roll the press scale, and the garnet gradient stops live twice
problem: The inventory duplicate is real: the same `setPress`/`pressVal`/cancel/`pressStyle` block appears twice. The gradient's stops belong to the gradient, yet each consumer restates them.
proposed: `usePressScale(enabled: boolean): { onPressIn; onPressOut; style }` in actions.tsx. `Gradient.garnet` becomes `{ colors, locations }` in `lib/tokens.ts`.
effect: about 20 lines go, and a third garnet surface cannot get the stops wrong.

title: `useCardRect` takes its mapper inputs from a private worklets field
problem: `__closure` is an internal of the worklets Babel plugin. If it is renamed or reshaped, the `?? {}` turns it into "no inputs".
proposed: `useCardRect(key, read, inputs: readonly SharedValue<unknown>[])`, with callers naming what `read` reads. Alternatively, a test that fails when `__closure` is absent on a worklet.
effect: the dependence on a library internal becomes explicit or guarded.

title: Notice timing puts a reading hold in `Motion` and ignores reduced motion for two shapes
problem: `chip` and `float` take `Motion.mark.{enter, hold, exit}` whatever `reduceMotion` is. `pill` goes through `motionMs("notice", reduceMotion)`. `hold: 1000` is a reading duration, which components/CLAUDE.md says belongs in `Reading`, not `Motion`.
proposed: `hold: Reading.mark`, and enter/exit via `motionMs("mark", reduceMotion)`.
effect: one rule for notice timing, and the token audit stops seeing a reading time in `Motion`.

title: Unused motion knob and component-literal durations
problem: A parameter with one value is a hypothetical seam. The two 500 ms literals are motion durations outside `Motion`, so they escape the reduced-motion and token checks.
proposed: drop the `durationMs` prop and use `SWEEP_MS`. Move both literals to `Motion.duration.*`.
effect: three fewer local knobs.

title: Rank letter-spacing is defined twice, and the joker rank ignores scale
problem: `LETTER_SPACING = -0.5` in cardFaceModel feeds `rankTextWidth`, which is the geometry that keeps index boxes from overlapping. CardView's stylesheet hardcodes `letterSpacing: -0.5` separately, so if one changes, the measured width no longer matches the painted width. `rankTextJoker` also pins `FontSize.xs` / `lineHeight: 12`, which overrides the scaled rank box.
proposed: import the constant into the style. Derive the joker size from the same scale.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: Render churn from fresh defaults and per-frame state
problem: The `placementPoints = {}` (357) and `disconnectedSeats = {}` (371) defaults are new objects on every render for replay, capture and bench callers. `placementPoints` is in the deps of the round-over effect in useTableFeedback (355), so that effect reruns on every render. `readExchange` returns a new object while an exchange is active (flightPhysics.ts:425-440), and that object is in the `tableA11yLabel` memo deps (GameTable 779).
proposed: hoist the defaults to module-level constants, key the memo on exchange fields, keep `hasMore` as state that is set only when it changes, and compute `shakeOffset` once.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: BenchScreen run latch has no finally
problem: `benchRunning` and the drain interval are reset only on the success path. A throw outside the per-scenario catch (`benchScenarios()`, diag, `recorder.postTo`) leaves the latch set forever and the interval running, and unmount does no cleanup. This is dev-only.
proposed: run the body in a non-hook helper with try/finally, and add an unmount cleanup effect.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: Platform branches scattered instead of behind one seam
problem: The web overflow-clip quirk (a focused child scrolls a `hidden` box) is written twice with two different casts: `GameTable.tsx:169-170` (`WEB_CLIP`, cast via `unknown as ViewStyle`) and `hand.tsx:1431` (`"clip" as "hidden"`). The "iOS cannot grey a view with a filter" quirk is split between `greyLayer.tsx:8-14` and `useLinkHold.ts:15-17, 76-80`, plus the `grey` prop doc at `feltCanvas.tsx:50`. `feltCanvas.tsx:57`'s `IOS` is a different quirk (opaque Skia).
proposed: `lib/platform.ts`: `export const clipOverflow: ViewStyle | null;` and `export const viewFilterGrey: boolean;`. `hapticsAvailable` exported from `lib/device/feedback.ts`. A `harnessData(state)` usable on Text and View.
effect: one place per quirk (about 8 sites); a new surface cannot get the cast wrong.

title: `useTableFeedback` recomputes the round and match outcome GameTable already has
problem: The 17-input interface exists to rebuild a value the caller holds. The sound and the visuals decide "outcome known" by different rules in two files. This is not shown to be a bug, but it is a locality problem.
proposed: `useTableFeedback({ ..., outcome: RoundOutcome, matchOutcome: RoundOutcome, scored: boolean })`, with `scored` decided once next to `roundOutcomeFor`.
effect: 7 inputs drop to 3; one rule for "decided".

title: Score pill and match-board derivation in GameTable
problem: pure geometry and labels sit in the component, beside the existing `components/table/scorePillModel.ts` and `lib/game/scorePill.ts`.
proposed: `pillAnchorFor(layout: TableLayout): PillAnchor` and `voteTop(anchor, open, scale)` in scorePillModel. `matchBoardFor(standings, players, winners, score, t)` in `lib/game/scorePill.ts`.
effect: about 45 lines become node-testable (`scorePillGeometry` and `scorePillStandings` already exist to extend).

title: `getComboLabel` is a pure label function living in a component, with a lossy key type
problem: `Record<string, TranslationKey>` loses exhaustiveness; an unknown type falls back to the raw `combo.type` string on screen.
proposed: move it to `components/table/spokenLabels.ts` (beside `lastPlayLabel`) as `Record<Combination["type"], TranslationKey>`.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: Animation-lifetime boilerplate
problem: 55 `cancelAnimation(` calls across components (`useTableFeedback.ts` 10, `hand.tsx` 9, `seats.tsx` 7, `moments.tsx` 7, `pile.tsx` 6, …). 11 of them are the exact `useEffect(() => () => cancelAnimation(x), [x])` shape. `hand.tsx:388-399` cancels 7 values by hand.
proposed: `useOwnedValue<T>(init: T): SharedValue<T>`, a shared value cancelled on unmount.
effect: About 25 cleanup effects removed, and "forgot to cancel" becomes structural. `tests/ui-rules/infiniteAnimations.test.ts` can accept the owned hook as the cancellation.

title: Both particle adapters re-state the per-frame scene step, and the web one never idles
problem: The seam between the two is real (Skia Atlas vs 2D canvas). But the step order sits in both adapters and must stay in lockstep by hand: `emberFrame` `coneRainFrame` `step` `stepAir`, with its moth trace `layout` `layoutMotes` `mothPose` The native adapter skips idle frames (`:92-94`). The web adapter clears and redraws every rAF tick forever, including at rest with no lit motes.
proposed: One worklet in `particleSprites.ts`: `stepScene(scene: {s: Particles; air: Air; ember: EmberRun; rain: RainRun}, l: AirLight, dt: number, reduced: boolean, rng: Rng, out: Float32Array): {lit: number; moth: MothPose | null; mothSet: boolean; idle: boolean}`. Each adapter keeps only its draw. The web loop returns early on `idle` the way native does.
effect: About 10 duplicated lines become one call. Web stops redrawing an idle table.

title: "Where the chips end" is computed in two places; computeScreenPads is a pass-through
problem: `notificationTopOffset` (tableFrame.ts:201-216) rebuilds the chip bottom from raw inputs: `max(PAD_TOP*s, topPad) + surplus + CHIP_H + PAD_INNER*s`. That is the same value as GameTable's banner band top, `frame.tableTop + CHIP_H(scale) + frame.pad` (GameTable.tsx:1386; tableTop at tableFrame.ts:153, pad at 165). NotificationBanner (96-103) works out `surplusHeight/2` again instead of reading the frame.
proposed: export one `chipsBottom(frame, scale)` from tableFrame.ts. Make `notificationTopOffset` take a `TableFrame`. Delete `computeScreenPads`.
effect: one source of truth for the band under the chips. A change to chip padding can no longer move the table and leave the banner behind.

title: Settings rows are spelled out six times
problem: every row repeats `row`/`stackRow > rowLeft > RowIcon + label/sublabel + control`. The inventory duplicates (267-281=284-309, 236-248=252-264, 237-246=270-279, 267-276=317-326) are real. The haptics capability check is restated in settingsSheet.tsx:304 (ui-F14).
proposed: `SettingRow({ icon, label, sublabel, stacked, children })`.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: Accessibility is mocked 46 times even though it has a public setter
problem: `setMotionPreference` (lib/accessibility.ts:18) is honoured by `usePrefersReducedMotion` (127). 18 files already use the setter. The other 46 mock the module, inconsistently: bannerBand:19, captureScreen:31 and homeReturnToTable:42 return `true` with preference `'off'`; matchOutcomeOnTheFelt:8 returns `false` with `'system'`.
proposed: delete the mocks; add `afterEach(() => setMotionPreference('system'))` in setup.ts; optionally a ui-rule banning `jest.mock('@/lib/accessibility')`.
effect: about 180 lines removed; the contradictory mock states disappear.
notes: Count differs: tests-T2 says 18 files use the setter, 07-tests-native finds 16; the 46 mocks are confirmed exactly.

title: The socket seam is untyped on both sides, and the integration helper's wire types have drifted
problem: Client: 17 hand-rolled fakes. 9 carry an identical lib/socket mock: acceptInviteClearsPending:30, friendLastSeen:28, friendRequestReconcile:38, friendRowArrivesWithTheBanner:38, sessionReplaced:33, signOutClearsQueryCache:21, socketAccountSwitch:25, socketContextFreshness:28, socketReconnect. 8 mock SocketContext instead (protocolMismatch:14, onlineAutoPass:11, rejoinFailed:24, …).
proposed: A typed `FakeSocket<S2C, C2S>` with `deliver(event, payload)`, `emitted(event)`, a real `off`, and an ack queue. `FakeIo` for the server, plus a `TableIo` port so handlers take the narrow emitter they use. `waitFor<E extends keyof ServerToClientEvents>(socket, event): Promise<Parameters<…>[0]>`.
effect: about 26 fakes become 1; 20 casts and about 90 lines go; 241 calls become type-checked, so wire drift fails `tsc`.
notes: CONTEXT.md records "no listener leak to fix"; the proposal is a typed fake, not a leak fix.

title: Reduced motion is guarded by four overlapping text scans; a motion seam would replace them
problem: Calls to Reanimated's `withTiming`, `withRepeat` and `withDelay` are scattered through components. Four tests then search the text for evidence that each call site consulted the reduce-motion preference or cancels on unmount. Two of the four pass on proximity alone.
proposed: A deep motion module (e.g. `lib/motion.ts`) that owns the vendor calls. Candidate interface: `timing(to, step, reduce: boolean)` `delayed(ms, anim)`, which always passes `ReduceMotion.System` `useLoop(sv, anim)`, which owns `cancelAnimation` on unmount Add `no-restricted-imports` of `withTiming`, `withRepeat` and `withDelay` from `react-native-reanimated` everywhere except that module, reusing the `paletteLayers` style at eslint.config.js:153-156.
effect: infiniteAnimations and withDelayReduceMotion are deleted. Most of reducedMotion is deleted.

title: The app contexts have no seam, so tests replace them with partial hand-typed mocks
problem: each mock is a partial, hand-typed value. A context gaining a field, or changing what a field means, passes every test that mocks it. Tests exercise the screen against an imagined provider, not the real one.
proposed: Export `AppProviders` from the layout, taking the HTTP transport (`apiRequest`) and a socket factory as props. `tests/native/harness/renderApp.tsx({route, user, socket: FakeSocket, http: FakeHttp, window})` mounts the real providers over fakes at the I/O edge. `<AuthProvider initialUser>` for signed-in starts.
effect: about 97 context mocks plus 28 I/O mocks deleted. Provider wiring becomes tested by every screen test.
notes: 07-tests-native-F3 contradicts the tests.md "Keep: slice hooks plus onlineContextMock" line: onlineContextMock still serves the legacy flat value to onlineRoundSelection, rejoinFailedExit and handMemo, so keeping it keeps two seams. tests.md lists it as keep.

title: Checks that exempt themselves or carry a spare exemption
problem: noFocusedTests:33 filters out its own file, so it does not check itself (a self-exempting safeguard). Use `blankCommentsAndStrings`, or move it to eslint (`jest/no-focused-tests`).
proposed: `blankCommentsAndStrings`, or move it to eslint (`jest/no-focused-tests`).
effect: Four exemptions go. The single-sourcing rule covers the CLAUDE.md files again.

title: Tests that write into the repo root or leak env changes
problem: A concurrent `git add`, or the root scan, picks up the fixture. rootScanRace exists because of this class. A failing assertion leaves the env changed for later tests in the same worker.
proposed: Use `mkdtempSync(os.tmpdir())` and pass a root, and wrap the env change in `try/finally`.
effect: Removes a flake class.

title: Assertions that cannot fail, or cannot tell the claim from its absence
problem: handTapStrip:34 `expect(strip / 2).toBeLessThan(strip)` is arithmetic on a positive number and is true whatever the component does. errorReporting:217-222 ("stops reporting once removed") asserts `listeners.size === 0` straight after the test itself called `listeners.clear()`. It cannot fail.
proposed: handTapStrip: assert the measured strip against the card height. errorReporting: unmount, or call the returned remover, then emit and assert nothing is reported. cardHitBox: assert the exact strip width.
effect: six false greens gone.

title: Timing constants copied into tests as prose
problem: each is a premise held in a comment. When production changes the value, these tests either keep passing at the wrong time window or fail without explaining why.
proposed: Export the constants: `REJOIN_RETRY_DELAY_MS`, `MAX_REJOIN_RETRIES`, `TRICK_WINNER_MS`, and the mark-enter duration. Import them in the tests. socketReconnect uses `reconnectDelayMs(0, () => 0.123)`.
effect: five drift sources go, and the exports gain test-only users (tolerable: they are timing contracts).

title: A live-network test and a machine-state test
problem: the result depends on network, auth or what is running on the machine, so the test is red offline or on a fork without a token and says nothing about the code.
proposed: move deleteBranchOnMerge to a scheduled repo-settings check, or skip it without GH_TOKEN and say so in the output. Point the reap test at the injected readTable, which workspace.test.ts:488-503 already uses.
effect: two environment-dependent tests become deterministic.

title: Store seam: one adapter, substituted by monkeypatching
problem: `userStore`, `roomStore` and `friendStore` are objects so tests can `t.mock.method` them (`roomStore.ts:50-55` says so). 19 non-store modules import `db` directly: `gamePersistence`, `ratings`, `replays`, `retention`, `stats`, `tableHandlers`, `userNames`, `admin` (13 queries), `authTokens`, `bugReports`, `clientErrors`, `deleteAccount`, `roundHistoryView`, `serverErrors`, `session`, `shutdown`, `events`, `push`, `ticket`. No PGlite or any second adapter exists.
proposed: Extend the deps-object pattern that already works here: roomLifecycleRaces:317 patches the deliberate `persistence` seam, and lobbyIntents and friendships take `deps` fakes. Apply it to friendStore, userStore and roomStore reads, and to rated-delta preview, in the modules that call them.
effect: turns about 12 monkeypatches into explicit adapters. Two adapters (prod plus test) make each one a real seam.

title: The nightly list is a regex copied into four places, plus 23 stub specs
problem: The parity spec regex is duplicated at playwright.config.ts:50 and playwright.parity.config.ts:8. Use a `*.parity.spec.ts` suffix instead.
proposed: a `*.parity.spec.ts` suffix instead.

title: Import-graph rules are kept in three text scans, one of which duplicates eslint, and none catches the violations the tools found

title: Native diagnostics module: unbounded buffer, state not reset between captures, error swallowed on stop
